Note for the staff file, written by Gurpreet, print-shop floor supervisor.

Maria came back on Monday after her diagnosis and told me, without fuss, what the doctor had asked her to do. She wrote it in a small notebook while we talked. Over the next few days I saw her set phone alarms for her next visit and the tests, and she keeps a blue folder of reports in her locker. When an alarm rings during a job, she steps aside for a minute, then returns.

I adjusted her Thursday shift so she can reach the clinic. I have not asked her about details and will not unless she brings them up. She looks tired some days but organised.

qa.q: Where does Maria keep her folder of reports?
qa.a: In her locker, and it is a blue folder.

qa.q: What might Maria be feeling when she steps aside for a minute as an alarm rings?
qa.a: She likely feels responsible and determined, taking her instructions seriously even if tired, and wanting to stay on top of care.

qa.q: What could Maria do if she missed an alarm one day, and why?
qa.a: She could check her notebook and folder and phone the clinic to rebook, because a routine has backups and a missed reminder is not the end of it.

qa.q: How does Gurpreet's Thursday change affect Maria?
qa.a: It gives Maria a way to keep her appointments without choosing between work and care, and not being questioned about details respects her privacy. 🙂

grounding: After a diagnosis, a person writes down the doctor's instructions, sets phone reminders and keeps reports in a folder.

passage:
Monday, 8 p.m. Kiran's diary.
It's official now. The doctor said it's a long-term thing and manageable if I follow the plan properly. I came home and cried for a while, then made tea and got organised, because crying wasn't going to remember anything for me.
What I did tonight:
1. Wrote the doctor's instructions in the front of this diary, word for word from the prescription sheet, including the foods to go easy on.
2. Set phone reminders for the medicines, the blood test on the 14th, and the follow-up on the 28th.
3. Put every report so far into a blue folder, dated, oldest at the back.
Tarun saw the folder and said, 'You've become an office.' He's also set a reminder on his own phone for the 14th so he can come with me.
It's a lot. But it's written down, so it's not all in my head.

qa.q: How did Kiran feel after coming home from the doctor?
qa.a: Upset enough to cry for a while, then steadier and determined once things were written down.

qa.q: What else could Kiran add to the routine?
qa.a: A page in the diary for questions to ask at the follow-up, noted as they come up.

qa.q: How does Tarun respond to the routine?
qa.a: Tarun teases gently about the folder, but backs it, setting a reminder to go along on the 14th.

grounding: Shows a young person after a diagnosis writing down the doctor's instructions, setting reminders for medicines and tests, and keeping a report folder.

Pranav: how did the follow-up go?
Lakshmi: good actually. the doctor said things are steadier
Pranav: 🎉 what changed
Lakshmi: honestly just doing what she said, properly this time
Lakshmi: first month I kept forgetting the medicine and missed a test
Pranav: I remember. you were so annoyed with yourself
Lakshmi: so now: phone alarms for medicines, calendar alerts for every test, and a folder with all reports in order
Lakshmi: I also wrote her instructions on a card stuck to the fridge
Pranav: the fridge card is very Amma
Lakshmi: it works though 😅
Pranav: next appointment?
Lakshmi: 12th. reminder already set. you coming?
Pranav: yes. setting one too
Lakshmi: thanks. it feels less scary when it's all in a system

qa.a: The 12th, with a reminder already set.

qa.q: How does Lakshmi feel about the system now?
qa.a: Relieved and more confident; it feels less scary with everything organised.

qa.q: What else could Lakshmi keep in the folder?
qa.a: A list of questions for each visit, and notes on anything that changes between appointments.

qa.q: How does Pranav see Lakshmi's progress?
qa.a: Pranav remembers how annoyed she was in the first month, celebrates the better follow-up and offers to come to the next one.

grounding: Shows a young person following a treatment plan with alarms, test reminders, a report folder and the doctor's instructions on the fridge.
